messages:
sam: FYI I tried to run terraform apply after splitting the remote state (moved staging resources into shared workspace) and the apply wants to destroy+recreate our ingress even though I didn't change the k8s manifest. plan excerpt below. anyone seen this after a state split?

laura: can you paste the exact plan lines? also which command did you use to move the state?

sam: pasted excerpt:
```
# kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app will be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_ingress" "redwood-app" {
  ~ metadata {
      ~ annotations = {
          - "cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer" = "letsencrypt" -> null
        }
    }
}
```
I moved state with `terraform state mv` from `module.staging.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app` to `module.shared.module.k8s.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app` (long story: split stacks). I also saw plan mention a provider change: provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes"] -> provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes"] (alias "staging").

josh: that alias thing is a red flag. If resource addresses moved under a different provider/config, Terraform treats that as a different resource. Did you preserve provider aliases and module paths exactly?

sam: I thought so but maybe not. `terraform state list | grep redwood-app` shows the new address but `terraform state show` looks different (annotations missing in state).

maya: this smells like external drift (cert-manager changed annotation) + address mismatch. Two approaches: 1) `terraform state mv` to correct address if the resource exists in the other workspace, or 2) import the live k8s resource into the new address: `terraform import module.shared.module.k8s.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app staging/redwood-app` and then `terraform plan`.

laura: before import, try `terraform refresh -target=module.shared.module.k8s.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app` to update state from the API. If refresh pulls the cert-manager annotation out of the resource then plan may stop wanting to replace.

sam: ran refresh, got a lock error: `Error: remote state is locked`

infra-bot: remote state locked by session `ci-runner-84` at 2025-09-12T18:12:03Z (operation in progress).

sam: ah — that CI job is from the deploy pipeline. I waited, then tried `terraform force-unlock 98a7f...` but it says "no active lock with ID". weird.

josh: sometimes the backend records a different lock ID; run `terraform state pull > state.json` and inspect the `lock` object (if using S3 backend with Dynamo or remote backend). Or check the deploy pipeline — if it's still running cancel it.

sam: deploy-bot shows a failed apply earlier, pipeline finished. I pulled state and there is a lingering `lock_id` field in the backend metadata (old session). I removed the Dynamo lock manually (we have a quick playbook in #eng-infra-runbooks) and then re-ran refresh.

sam: after refresh the plan still wants to replace because the state address is `module.shared.module.k8s.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app` but the live resource name in k8s is `staging/redwood-app` (same) — the provider alias in the config changed path. I think when splitting the state I accidentally used a different provider alias `provider.kubernetes.staging` vs `provider.kubernetes` causing the provider ID to differ.

laura: solution: move the state resource back to the exact address Terraform expects (or adjust the provider alias). Example: `terraform state mv 'module.shared.module.k8s.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app' 'module.shared.module.k8s.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app'` (if address mismatch subtle) — or better: `terraform state rm <old>` then `terraform import <new> <k8s id>` if the mv can't reconcile provider meta.

maya: also consider `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` for this ingress if cert-manager keeps mutating annotations; that prevents churn. But that's a policy change so coordinate with app owners.

sam: going to `terraform import module.shared.module.k8s.kubernetes_ingress.redwood-app staging/redwood-app` and then `terraform plan -out=fix.plan`. will apply only if plan clean.

deploy-bot: apply job started for workspace `shared` by @sam (CI #8421) :hourglass:

sam: import succeeded, plan is clean now (no replace). applying.

deploy-bot: apply failed: provider config mismatch for provider "registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes" (alias "staging"). See logs: `Failed to find provider "kubernetes" with alias "staging" for module.shared.module.k8s`.

josh: that means the configuration in current workspace doesn't define the alias. Either add the provider alias back in config or re-import into the provider that exists. For a quick unblock, define a provider alias in `providers.tf`:
```hcl
provider "kubernetes" {
  alias = "staging"
  config_path = var.kubeconfig_staging
}
```
and `terraform init -upgrade` then re-run apply.

sam: added alias, re-ran init, apply completed :party-parrot:

laura: nice. follow-up: create a short runbook for state-splits documenting provider alias rules + prefer `terraform import` over moving addresses when provider meta differs. Put it in `#eng-infra-runbooks`.

sam: will do. marking this resolved. thanks all :thumbsup:
